mechanism: Foscarnet causes dose-dependent nephrotoxicity and electrolyte wasting (including hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia), while chlorthalidone is a thiazide-like diuretic that also causes potassium and magnesium depletion, compounding electrolyte abnormalities and increasing risk of cardiac arrhythmias.
action: Monitor serum electrolytes (particularly potassium and magnesium) frequently; consider alternative antihypertensive agent or reduce chlorthalidone dose; ensure adequate hydration during foscarnet therapy and consider potassium/magnesium supplementation.
